To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: URGENT – stop using Brightline Pro 6% developer, batch LX2291

Please check your developer before doing any more colour. Kelvin Trade say a filling error means bottles labelled Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L, batch LX2291, may actually contain 12% (40 vol) developer. That is double the strength on the label.

The affected batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November. Other batches and strengths are not affected according to Kelvin Trade.

This has already caused a serious problem here. A client’s scalp was burnt on Saturday while a bottle from this batch was being used, and the hair lifted much faster than normal. Another renter had foils getting roasting hot and unusually fast lift on Thursday, which she initially put down to the heater. This is a safety issue, not just an “inconvenience”.

HOW TO CHECK YOUR BOTTLES

- Look at the BASE OF THE BOTTLE for the batch code. It is not on the box, so checking the box alone is no use.
- Stop using anything marked LX2291 immediately, including opened and part-used bottles.
- Check the open bottles in your trolley as well as unopened stock in the back, cupboards and anywhere else you keep colour.
- Put affected bottles somewhere separate and clearly mark them DO NOT USE so nobody picks one up by mistake.

WHAT TO LOOK OUT FOR

Because it may be 12% rather than 6%, it can lift much faster than expected, over-process the hair and leave it dry, damaged or at greater risk of breakage. Colour may come out uneven, patchy or brassy. Foils can become excessively hot. Clients may feel unexpected heat, strong tingling or burning, and the stronger developer can cause redness and chemical burns to the scalp.

A patch test does not make this batch safe to use. The problem is the strength in the bottle.

IF SOMEBODY REACTS IN THE CHAIR

- Stop the service straight away. Do not leave it processing to see if the sensation settles.
- Wear gloves and rinse immediately with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water. No shampoo, toner, creams, aloe or other chemicals on the area. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible.
- For a suspected chemical burn, call 999 for medical help immediately. Do not wait for blistering or severe pain. Continue rinsing for about an hour and follow the call handler’s instructions. Chemical burns need hospital assessment.
- Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also require 999 immediately.
- Once everybody is safe, record it in the incident book at the desk, with the product, batch, timings and what happened. Take dated photos where appropriate.

NHS first-aid guidance: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/

RETURNS AND BOTTLES TO KEEP

The Kelvin Trade rep is in on Tuesday 10 November and affected bottles can be handed back to him, or taken to their Hillington depot, for full credit.

If you have had a reaction, a suspected burn or another problem with a bottle, KEEP THAT BOTTLE BACK. Do not bin it and do not hand it back with the returns, even if it is part-used or empty. Keep it safely with the batch code visible and take a photo of the base.

Please check today, and if you have had unusually fast lift, very hot foils or a client reacting since 19 October, check whether you still have the bottle before assuming it was your mix, timing or the heater.

Kirsty
